title: Negative Keywords on Amazon: The Most Overlooked Tactic Your Agency Sh | Houzz Forum
text: Your auto campaign has been running for four months. You pulled the search term report last week and found that $800 in ad spend went to "yoga mat bag" clicks on your sports water bottle listing. Zero conversions. You're selling water bottles. Buyers looking for yoga mat bags have no interest in your product. That $800 is gone. And without a systematic negative keyword process, next month will look similar. Negative keyword management is unglamorous work. It doesn't appear in case studies or agency pitch decks. But it's one of the most reliable ways to improve ACoS — and most Amazon sellers aren't doing it systematically. Why Negative Keywords Matter More Than Most Sellers Realize? Amazon's auto campaigns match your product to search queries based on listing content. The algorithm is broad and opportunistic. It will match your listing to adjacent and sometimes completely irrelevant queries if it detects any keyword overlap. Those matches generate impressions, sometimes clicks, and almost never purchases. Every click from an irrelevant search query is wasted spend. Over weeks and months, these waste clicks add up to a meaningful percentage of total ad spend producing zero revenue. The cumulative ACoS impact of eliminating irrelevant clicks compounds over time. The search term report is your evidence base. It shows you every search query that triggered one of your ads, how many clicks it generated, and what it converted. Queries with multiple clicks and zero conversions are either irrelevant or reveal a listing problem. Either way, they're costing money they shouldn't. An amazon ads agency handling your account should review search term reports and add negative keywords systematically — not just when performance problems are obvious. Negative keyword management is like expense management. No individual waste item seems important enough to prioritize. But the cumulative savings across all waste items are significant and compound indefinitely once captured. Building a Negative Keyword Discovery Workflow Weekly Search Term Report Review Pull your search term report weekly for all active campaigns — not monthly. High-spend, low-converting queries that run for four weeks without a negative added represent significant accumulated waste. A weekly review cycle catches them early. Sort the report by spend descending. The most expensive non-converting queries are your priority targets. A query that's generated $50 in spend and zero conversions is more important to negative than one that's generated $5. Conversion-Based Threshold Criteria Set explicit criteria for when a search term becomes a negative candidate. A common framework: Explicit criteria prevent inconsistent application and ensure the workflow runs mechanically rather than relying on subjective review. Campaign-Level vs. Ad Group-Level Placement Negative keywords can be added at the campaign level (blocking across all ad groups in a campaign) or the ad group level (blocking only within a specific ad group). Campaign-level negatives are appropriate for broad irrelevance — a query that's irrelevant to your entire campaign. Ad group-level negatives are appropriate when a query might be relevant in one ad group but not another. Match Type Considerations Negative exact match blocks only that precise query. Negative phrase match blocks any query containing that phrase. Choose match type based on how broadly you need to block: Be cautious with broad negative phrase blocking — it can inadvertently block relevant queries that contain similar words. Proactive Negative List Building Beyond reactive search term report review, agencies should build proactive negative lists from the start of a campaign. Before launching, identify the most obvious irrelevant query categories for your product type. A children's toy brand should immediately add adult category negatives. A premium product should add "cheap" and "budget" as negatives from day one. A brand-specific product should negative competitor brand names to prevent wasted spend from searchers who aren't considering switching. These proactive negatives save the spend that would otherwise go to learning that these queries don't convert — spend that never needed to happen. Frequently Asked Questions What is negative keyword management and why is it critical for Amazon PPC? Negative keyword management involves identifying and blocking irrelevant search queries that trigger your ads but don't convert. Every click from an irrelevant query wastes ad spend, and these waste clicks compound over months—making systematic negative keyword management one of the most reliable ways to improve ACoS, even though it's often overlooked. How often should you review search term reports for negative keywords? You should pull and review search term reports weekly for all active campaigns, not monthly. Weekly reviews catch high-spend, low-converting queries early before they accumulate significant wasted budget over four weeks or longer. What threshold criteria should you use to identify negative keyword candidates? A common framework is three or more clicks with zero conversions as a trigger to review query relevance. You should prioritize by spend descending, focusing first on the most expensive non-converting queries—for example, a query that generated $50 in spend with zero conversions is a higher priority negative than one that cost $5. How does Amazon's auto campaign algorithm contribute to irrelevant clicks? Amazon's auto campaigns match products to search queries based on listing content using a broad algorithm that detects keyword overlap. The system is opportunistic and will match your listing to adjacent and sometimes completely irrelevant queries if it finds any content similarity, generating impressions and clicks from buyers searching for entirely different products. Why should you work with an Amazon ads agency for negative keyword management? An experienced Amazon PPC agency handles weekly search term report reviews systematically across all campaigns, catching wasteful queries before they accumulate significant spend. This ongoing, disciplined approach to negative keyword discovery is rare among individual sellers and represents a meaningful competitive advantage in cost management. Tracking the Impact of Negative Keyword Management Measure your waste percentage — spend on zero-conversion queries as a percentage of total spend — monthly. A well-managed account should have a declining waste percentage over time as the negative keyword library grows. A flat or rising waste percentage indicates the workflow isn't running consistently. The cumulative savings from systematic negative keyword management over a twelve-month engagement are significant. The agencies that track and demonstrate this impact on a monthly basis are the ones treating negative keyword management as a strategic function rather than housekeeping. Make sure yours does.

Visual content enables individuals to widely punctuate aspects of their identity, whether that involves life, fashion, trips, achievements, or aesthetic sensibilities. As Goffman’s proposition of the “ donation of tone ”( 1959) posits, social life involves managing our tone to impact how others perceive us. This “ aesthetic identity ” communicates not just taste but also values, intentions, and belonging within specific social mores. For illustration, minimalistic feeds suggest simplicity and fineness, while various, vibrant feeds may reflect creativity or extroversion. Hashtags and community engagement further support identity construction. By tagging prints with specific expressions or sharing in trends, druggies gesture cooperation with certain groups, testaments, or cultures. These digital labels also serve as symbols in offline communities, allowing individuals to claim class or recognition within curated social spheres.
